links.comparator_used: Prompt B, which asked for patient-targeted uveitis information easy to understand by an average American, with no grade level or FKGL instruction
links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of generated uveitis patient information (lower is easier to read)
links.effect: Both models produced lower FKGL with prompt A (6th-grade/FKGL instruction) than prompt B, but the difference was significant only for ChatGPT (P < 0.0001). Mean FKGL with prompt A: ChatGPT 6.3 ± 1.2, Bard 10.5 ± 0.8.
links.quote: ChatGPT and Bard generated responses with lower FKGL scores (i.e., easier to understand) in response to prompt A compared with prompt B.

links.comparator_used: Original online uveitis health information from first-page Google results (mean FKGL 11.0 ± 1.4)
links.outcome: FKGL of rewritten versus original online uveitis health information
links.effect: ChatGPT lowered mean FKGL from 11.0 ± 1.4 to 8.0 ± 1.0 (P < 0.0001). Bard did not lower it (mean FKGL 11.1 ± 1.6).
links.tradeoff: ChatGPT's rewrites (mean FKGL 8.0) still did not reach the requested 6th-grade level. Bard did not simplify the text.
links.quote: ChatGPT lowered the FKGL to 8.0 ± 1.0 (P < 0.0001) when asked to rewrite the content.
